description: Contract-First design — agent writes interface contract before implementation
scenario: User asks for a Task API. Agent should first write the TypeScript interface contract (TaskAPI) with method signatures and types before any implementation code.
expected_outcome: Agent writes a typed interface with createTask, listTasks, getTask, updateTask, deleteTask methods with proper input/output types

description: Consistent error semantics — agent uses uniform error format
scenario: User asks for error handling on a REST API endpoint. Agent should produce a single consistent error shape (code, message, details) used across all endpoints.
expected_outcome: Agent produces a single APIError interface and uses it consistently in error responses with proper HTTP status codes

description: Validation boundaries — agent validates at system edges only
scenario: User asks to add input validation to an API. Agent should validate at the route handler boundary using a schema parser, not scatter validation throughout internal code.
expected_outcome: Agent validates at the API boundary using safeParse/zod/validators, then trusts internal code without re-validation

description: Idempotency key implementation — agent implements atomic idempotency guard
scenario: User asks to make a payment endpoint idempotent. Agent should implement an idempotency key mechanism with atomic claim via unique constraint, not check-then-insert race pattern.
expected_outcome: Agent implements idempotency with atomic unique constraint claim (not TOCTOU pattern), payload validation on reuse, and explicit in-flight strategy

description: Additive changes — agent extends interface without breaking consumers
scenario: An existing API needs a new 'priority' field. Agent should add it as optional (backward compatible), not modify existing field types or remove fields.
expected_outcome: Agent adds the new field as optional, preserves all existing required fields with their original types
